7.1.	 QUALITY CONTROL TESTS FOR RADIOGRAPHERS
visible_text: TABLE 8. SUMMARY OF QUALITY CONTROL TESTS (cont.)
Section	Title	Equipment	Tolerance	Frequency	Reference
3.2.1	Verification of beam collimation	Phantom, computed radiography plate or self-developing film	±2% of SID	Annual	[14]
3.2.2	Verification of beam geometry	Alignment test objects, attenuator, computed radiography plate or self-developing film	Alignment: ±2% SID; Centring: ±1% SID	Annual	[4, 5]
3.2.3	Verification of different field sizes	Phantom	±2% of SID	Annual	[14]
3.2.4	Patient ESAK rate	Ionization chamber or solid state detector, PMMA slabs	Manufacturer’s specifications or 88 mGy/min (normal mode); 176 mGy/min (high dose rate mode)	Annual	[5, 6, 8, 9, 11]
3.2.5	Image receptor ESAK rate	Ionization chamber or solid state detector, 25 mm Al slab, Cu plates	0.2–1 μGy/s (with Al, 70–80 kV); ±25% of baseline	Annual	[4, 7]
visual_relations: The table is structured with six columns: Section, Title, Equipment, Tolerance, Frequency, Reference. Each row corresponds to a specific QC test (sections 3.2.1–3.2.5). The 'Tolerance' column contains compound entries for sections 3.2.2 and 3.2.5, with multiple conditions separated by line breaks or semicolons. The 'Equipment' column lists measurement tools and phantoms. The 'Reference' column cites numbered sources in square brackets.
units: % of SID
mGy/min
μGy/s
mm
kV
uncertainties: ±2% of SID
±1% SID

summary: This page (p. 189) continues Table 8, summarizing five quality control tests for radiographic equipment: beam collimation (3.2.1), beam geometry (3.2.2), field size verification (3.2.3), patient ESAK rate (3.2.4), and image receptor ESAK rate (3.2.5). All tests are performed annually. Tolerances are specified relative to SID (source-to-image distance) or as absolute dose rates, with references cited for each test.

6.2.	 QUALITY CONTROL TESTS FOR MEDICAL PHYSICISTS
visible_text: TABLE 6. SUGGESTED TIME FRAME FOR CORRECTIVE ACTIONS
Immediate action	Action within 30 days
Room temperature not controlled	Angulation indicator not functioning
Loose parts, paddles damaged or bucky not clean	Gantry motion not smooth
Hoses or cables kinked or damaged	Faulty panel switches, pedals, indicator lights and meters
Interlocks faulty	Laser or light inoperative
Time, date or facility identification incorrect or not present in the image	Current technique chart not posted
Cleaning solution not available	Operator radiation shield damaged
Automatic and/or manual compression release not working (mammography only)

6.2. QUALITY CONTROL TESTS FOR MEDICAL PHYSICISTS
6.2.1. Image display systems
6.2.1.1. Description and objective
The quality of the image display and the associated viewing conditions for the acquisition console and workstations are tested to ensure the following:
(a) The image is represented without distortions and in the appropriate size;
(b) The room illuminance and display reflection and the luminance response are set properly;
(c) The display resolution, low and high contrast and display noise are within tolerances.
An updated guide for display QA was published by the AAPM [30] during the preparation of this handbook. It is suggested to consider the most recent version for the revision of the local QA programme.
visual_relations: Table 6 is a two-column table with headers 'Immediate action' and 'Action within 30 days'. Each row pairs a specific equipment or environmental issue with its required corrective timeframe. Below the table, section headings 6.2, 6.2.1, and 6.2.1.1 introduce the topic of image display system quality control, repeating the same three objectives (a–c) as in the nearby text. The table appears on page 161, as indicated by the page number at bottom right.
units: No explicit units are present in the visible text or table; timeframes are given as 'Immediate' and 'within 30 days'.
uncertainties: The table contains duplicated entries in the original nearby text (e.g., 'Faulty panel switches...' and 'Interlocks faulty' appear twice), but the clean version in the image shows each item only once. The phrase 'Current technique chart not posted' appears under 'Action within 30 days', while 'Cleaning solution not available' is listed under 'Immediate action'—no justification or tolerance limits are provided in the visible content. The reference '[30]' to AAPM is cited but not defined here.
summary: This page presents Table 6, which categorizes equipment and environmental issues requiring corrective actions into two timeframes: immediate or within 30 days. It also introduces Section 6.2.1 on image display system quality control, outlining three key objectives related to geometric fidelity, viewing conditions (illuminance, reflection, luminance), and display performance (resolution, contrast, noise). A reference to an updated AAPM guide ([30]) is included for display QA program updates.

Structures that cause this dense shadowing artefact by blocking sound wave transmission include 
cortical bone, gallstones, kidney stones, uterine fibroids, intrauterine devices, surgical clips and 
calcifications in organs like the thyroid gland.
Shadowing from calcified structures like stones cause a hard black shadow or band that descends 
in a straight path deep to the structure causing it. Shadowing produced by stones, aids in stone 
detection and diagnosis. This ‘clean’ shadowing is distinguished from the ‘dirty’ shadowing often 
seen from bowel gas (see gas artefacts).
